cells.tense: You are here now, reading the whole shape while still standing inside it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you understand well and sketch its shape on a page, clear enough to hand over.
cells.core:
The whole shape arrives for you before you can explain how you know — a system, a group, a person's situation — and you aren't forcing it. You're reading from inside rather than judging from a distance, so what you see holds up when you check it against the parts.
What's easy to miss is how much of this is holding steady, and how quietly it works. Let it feed something concrete: a conversation where you say the shape of a problem out loud, or a decision where you trust the whole read instead of gathering more pieces first. Hold the whole thing and the people in it, and what you say stays honest without turning cold.

cells.tense: You are bracing for the moment the pattern finally makes sense to the room.
cells.ask: Say the pattern once, cleanly, to one person, then stop talking and let it sit.
cells.core:
You've gone deep enough to see how the pieces fit, and now you want the room to see it too. You push the whole shape at people before they've asked, mapping their situation for them, getting ahead of where they actually stand. The depth is real. The delivery is running ahead of the moment.
Somewhere in you is a sense that if you stop forcing the pattern outward, it won't land. But a well-made shape doesn't need pushing — it needs claiming, once, clearly. Make the structure visible, then let it stand. People walk into a shape that holds, and they walk in faster when nobody's standing over them explaining it.

cells.tense: You stopped drawing the whole shape back when the room didn't meet it.
cells.ask: Describe one thing you understand to someone new, in ordinary words, and leave it there.
cells.core:
There's a depth in you that isn't getting used. You notice connections and whole shapes, but saying the big picture has gone quiet, and you've been holding it closer since. That habit of noticing hasn't gone anywhere. What stopped is handing it over.
What's running low isn't your mind — it's the shared half of understanding. Meaning gets solid for you when someone else holds part of it. So don't try to force the depth back. Give one piece of what you understand to someone, in plain words, even badly, and let them keep it. Contact wakes this up faster than sitting alone with it will.

cells.tense: You are already reading the whole shape and calling it just how things are.
cells.ask: Mark one read you made as your own — tell one person it was yours, once.
cells.core:
This is already running. When something clicks together, when you know how the pieces fit before anyone explains them, that's the pattern showing itself to you — and it happens often enough that you've stopped noticing it as something you do. It feels like the truth simply being true.
The reading is running fine. What's missing is credit. When the shape gets called how things are, instead of what you see, the situation gets the credit and you get nothing. Try naming one of those moments as yours, out loud, to one person. Not to brag. To put your name back on the thing you actually did.
